program_name: Nutrition MS (Plan A thesis / Plan B)
department_or_school: Department of Food Science and Nutrition, College of Food, Agricultural and Natural Resource Sciences (CFANS)
spring_2027_deadline: Not posted. The FScN admissions page lists only 'Spring 2026: September 15' for Nutrition, so the program has a spring intake. If the date is unchanged, the Spring 2027 deadline (2026-09-15) has already passed as of 2026-10-11. Confirm with the department.
fall_2027_deadline: Not posted. The Fall 2026 Nutrition deadline was December 4 (FScN admissions page). The 2027 date is not yet posted. If the date is unchanged, expect about 2026-12-04; confirm.
funding_deadline_note: No separate funding deadline was seen. Department awards (e.g. the Caldwell Fellowship) are listed on the FScN financial aid awards page. Whether every admit is considered automatically is Not verified.
ielts_subscore_note: Graduate School (Twin Cities) English page, per search summary: IELTS 6.5 total, 6.5 writing, 6.5 reading. The page says programs may require higher scores. FScN says the English test is a University requirement 'not enforced by the Department of Food Science and Nutrition.' Sana's subscores are unknown; check that writing and reading are each 6.5 or higher.
funding_summary: FScN Graduate Student Financial Aid Awards page: Caldwell Fellowship (for FScN students; covers tuition and health insurance and provides a stipend at 110% of the standard FScN graduate assistant pay rate); Nutrition-targeted awards including the Alice Biester Assistantship, Novartis Nutrition Research Assistantship and Matsan Nutrition Scholarship (Matsan is for students planning to sit for the RDN exam). UMN graduate assistantships include tuition benefits (except summer) covering tuition and all or part of the University fee according to appointment percentage. Graduate School funding page: most graduate assistantships are not posted publicly and are reserved for students in the department's programs. FScN tuition page: 2025-2026 full-time (6-14 credits) nonresident tuition $16,776 per semester. Guaranteed funding for admits: Not verified.
notes: IMPORTANT FOR OUTREACH: the FScN Nutrition admissions information says prospective students are discouraged from contacting prospective advisors before advancing to the second round of application review, to keep initial review unbiased. Do NOT cold-email UMN FScN Nutrition faculty before that stage. Questions go to the Graduate Programs Coordinator (Andrew Howe, FScN staff page) or the Director of Graduate Studies (Chi Chen). Program page statistics: average fall applicants 14.8, average fall admits 9.8, average applicant GPA 3.62. Most fall admission decisions are sent February-April. Applications go through the UMN Graduate School central system and can be submitted before all recommendation letters arrive, but letters must arrive by the deadline. The search summary did not say whether the MS listed as degree_level is Plan A (thesis) or Plan B; both appear to exist. The integrated BS/MS Plan B (May 1 deadline) is only for current UMN FScN undergraduates and does not apply.

program_name: Public Health Nutrition MPH (Standard track and Coordinated Master's Program track)
department_or_school: Division of Epidemiology and Community Health, School of Public Health
spring_2027_deadline: Not verified. The SPH deadline table lists only fall-term deadlines for this program.
fall_2027_deadline: December 1 priority/scholarship deadline; May 15 final deadline (Standard and Coordinated tracks; SOPHAS application complete by 11:59 p.m. Eastern). The pages do not name the cycle year; confirm they apply to Fall 2027 (expected 2026-12-01 priority and 2027-05-15 final).
funding_deadline_note: School-wide scholarship priority deadline December 1: admitted applicants whose SOPHAS application is complete and verified by then get first-round school-wide scholarship consideration. Later awards are rolling, based on available funds.
ielts_subscore_note: SPH International Applicants page: IELTS 'preferred minimum total score: 7.0'. Scores go to SOPHAS (HAMPCAS does not accept official IELTS). Test date must be within 24 months of program start. The requirement is waived after 16 semester (24 quarter) credits at an accredited US or Canadian English-medium institution within 24 months, excluding ESL coursework. Sana's 6.5 is below the preferred 7.0. Whether 6.5 is considered is Not verified; ask sph-admissions or retake.
toefl_min: TOEFL iBT preferred minimum total 100 (tests before 2026-01-21); the page lists 5 for tests on or after 2026-01-21, apparently the new TOEFL band scale; confirm.
funding_summary: PHN MPH cost page: Maternal and Child Nutrition Traineeships are for U.S. citizens only (Sana is not eligible). The program awards 3-5 Research Assistantship positions. Endowed scholarships (Ruth Stief, Marguerite Queneau, Alyce Stang) require the RD credential plus at least one year of work experience. 2026-2027 MPH tuition is per credit: $1,668 non-resident ($1,268 resident) for fall/spring. SPH says graduate assistantships provide tuition benefits and wages and can also be found after enrolling. No guaranteed full funding was seen.
notes: Applies through SOPHAS. Coordinated Program (dietetics) applicants must also apply through DICAS, after submitting SOPHAS. Prerequisites listed for the traditional track: a human biology course, a general chemistry course and an introduction to human nutrition. The school-wide table shows a general fall final deadline of August 1, which conflicts with the program-specific May 15; the program-specific date governs. The IELTS preferred minimum (7.0) is above Sana's 6.5. An MPH is a professional degree with limited funding, so it is a weaker fit for a fully funded goal.
